title: Interleaved-batch memory safety & soft-GC: detection and mitigations
author: Laura Kim
body:
Summary:

This document describes a class of hard-to-reproduce memory-safety failures that we observed in production during sustained mixed workloads: a combination of interleaved (asynchronous + synchronous) batching, aggressive KV-cache soft garbage collection (soft-GC), and fast slot recycling can produce illegal memory accesses and occasional kernel crashes. The net result is transient instance instability, sporadic OOMs on GPUs, and elevated tail latency as affected shards restart.

Background: why this class appears

- Our runtime performs continuous batching with two execution paths: synchronous (hotpath) and asynchronous (background coalesced batches).
- A soft-GC subsystem attempts to reclaim KV-cache memory opportunistically when host- or device-memory pressure grows; it marks entries stale and reclaims in the background without global synchronization to avoid latency cliffs.
- Worker slot recycling reclaims CPU/GPU slot metadata aggressively to maximize throughput. When these three systems interleave at the wrong time, reclaimed GPU-side buffers or stream handles can be referenced by an in-flight kernel, leading to illegal memory access and CUDA driver errors.

Observed symptoms (production signals)

- Sporadic GPU kernel failures (CUDA errors logged: UNKNOWN or illegal memory access) without obvious memory growth prior to failure.
- Increase in tail latency and 5xx error spike in model-serving routes that use long KV cache lifetimes (chat sessions).
- Short-lived pod restarts on a small percentage (~0.3%–1%) of nodes; restart reason = crashloop at the GPU driver layer.
- Traces show kernel launch times overlapped with cache-evict markers and slot-reuse timestamps.

Known reproducibility steps (local repro)

1. Use a synthetic client that alternates short synchronous requests (prompt length 16–32) with long-generation asynchronous requests (prompt length 512+) to force mixed batching paths.
2. Configure a small device-memory headroom to trigger soft-GC: set kv_cache_soft_gc_threshold = 0.78 and kv_cache_eviction_batch_size = 16.
3. Reduce slot_reuse_delay_ms to a small value (10ms) to emulate aggressive recycling.
4. Run the workload with a high concurrency driver until you observe intermittent CUDA errors.

Telemetry and detection rules

- Important signals to capture (add to node-level dashboards):
  - cuda_error_count (per GPU): alerts when > 0 in 5m window
  - kv_cache_eviction_rate and kv_cache_reclaim_time_p50/p95
  - slot_reuse_rate and slot_reuse_delay_ms distribution
  - kernel_launch_overlap_ratio: fraction of launches that overlap with a cache-reclaim marker (sampled)

- Detection rule (recommended):
  - Alert if cuda_error_count > 0 OR kernel_launch_overlap_ratio > 0.1 for a given shard AND kv_cache_eviction_rate_p95 > baseline + 3 sigma.

Immediate mitigations (for oncall)

1. Throttle soft-GC: admin API

   curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"kv_cache_soft_gc_threshold": 0.92, "kv_cache_eviction_batch_size": 4}' https://admin.internal/runtime/config

   Effect: reduces background reclaim aggressiveness and gives in-flight kernels more time to complete.

2. Increase slot reuse delay to force explicit fencing:

   curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"slot_reuse_delay_ms": 250}' https://admin.internal/runtime/config

   Effect: prevents immediate reuse of CPU/GPU slot structs while kernels or stream callbacks may still hold references.

3. If alerting indicates a specific node / shard: cordon the node and redeploy the runtime with the mitigations above; optionally drain and restart the affected pod to clear dangling state.

Long-term fixes (engineering roadmap)

- Short-term (sprint-scale):
  1) Add explicit device-side fencing and reference counting for KV cache buffers. Before reclaiming, ensure all stream callbacks have executed and kernel completion fences are observed.
  2) Make soft-GC cooperative: transition from blind background reclamation to a token-based protocol where a limited number of concurrent reclaims can happen per-shard.
  3) Add stronger sanitizers in the dev profiling harness to catch races (e.g., ASAN-like host checks and CUDA memcheck in staging).

- Mid-term (quarter-scale):
  1) Introduce a kernel-scheduling handshake that timestamps reclaim windows and prevents kernel launches that would reference recently reclaimed buffers.
  2) Improve batch planner to prefer contiguous execution (avoid interleaving synchronous launches with async coalesced batches when soft-GC is active).
  3) Add automated tests in the benchmarking suite that run mixed-workload tortures for >8 hours and report divergence metrics.

Impact to release & rollout notes

- Releases that change KV cache layout, soft-GC heuristics, or slot metadata must include:
  - Benchmark matrix results for mixed-sync/async workloads (see Mixed-Workload Stress Matrix).
  - Profiling traces demonstrating zero kernel-reclaim overlap for p99 windows.
  - New canary policy requiring 48h of shadow traffic with injected GC pressure.

Benchmarking & profiling guidance

- Use the 'mixed-batcher-stress' scenario in the benchmark suite with these knobs:

  - concurrency: 64
  - sync_fraction: 0.35
  - generation_length: 512
  - kv_cache_hard_limit_fraction: 0.82

- Profiling checklist:
  1) Capture kernel launch timestamps and GC marker timestamps in high-resolution traces.
  2) Export per-kernel stream id and buffer UUID (instrumentation) to facilitate matching.
  3) Run CUDA memcheck on a small sample to detect illegal access (use in staging-only due to perf overhead).

Scheduler & kernel implications

- Scheduler adjustments to consider:
  - Introduce a soft barrier token that prevents certain asynchronous batch types from starting while a reclaim token is held.
  - Track per-shard outstanding device-side references and decrement at kernel callback completion; disallow reclaim until zero.

Minimal config reference (table)

| key | suggested safe default | description |
|-----|------------------------|-------------|
| kv_cache_soft_gc_threshold | 0.90 | fraction of device memory used before soft-GC steps up |
| kv_cache_eviction_batch_size | 4 | number of entries evicted per async GC cycle |
| slot_reuse_delay_ms | 200 | delay before a freed slot can be reused |
| max_concurrent_kernels | 128 | cap on concurrent kernel launches per GPU |

Runbook: triage checklist (oncall)

1. Confirm signal: check cuda_error_count and kernel_launch_overlap_ratio.
2. If cuda errors present: flip mitigations (throttle soft-GC and increase slot_reuse_delay_ms).
3. Isolate affected node(s): mark unschedulable; rotate traffic if more than one node impacted.
4. Collect traces: attach last 15 minutes of kernel/GPU traces and KV GC logs and upload to incident artifact store.
5. If errors persist after mitigations: open high-priority SEV and page runtime-kernel team.

Post-incident follow-ups

- Create a dedicated test in the benchmark suite labeled mixed-gc-safety and run in CI-nightly until flakiness is resolved.
- Add regression alert: any release that modifies kv_cache_* or slot_* config keys must run the mixed-gc-safety scenario.
- Schedule an architecture review to approve the kernel-scheduling handshake proposal.

Owners and escalation path

- Primary owner: runtime-kernel (eng team) — Laura Kim (author)
- Secondary: runtime-observability — Diego Morales
- Escalation: oncall -> runtime-kernel lead -> eng-sre -> CTO pager if > 3h impact on customer SLAs.

References and artifacts

- Reproducer repo: //git.internal/repro/mixed-gc-safety (staging-only)
- Relevant dashboards: GPU / KV Cache / Kernel Overlap (dash IDs in related_pages)
- Follow-up ADR: (planned) kernel-fence-and-refcount-adr (link to be added after review)

Appendix: quick debug commands

- Tail summarized kernel overlap events:
  kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=serving -c kernel-inspector --since=15m | grep OVERLAP | jq -r '.msg' | head -n 200

- Increase soft-GC threshold temporarily from kubernetes config map:
  kubectl edit cm runtime-config -n runtime
  # set kv_cache_soft_gc_threshold: 0.92

Contact the runtime-kernel team in #runtime-kernel on Slack for fast assistance.
